name: Mario Rodriguez
title: Chief Product Officer
bio: Mario Rodriguez leads GitHub's product organization and the company's AI strategy. He previously led the GitHub Copilot product line, launching and scaling it across thousands of organizations and millions of developers, and led GitHub's Enterprise business, which serves more than 90% of the Fortune 100. He has also been responsible for GitHub's core developer productivity services including repositories, pull requests, and issues. Mario joined GitHub following Microsoft's acquisition of the company, after more than a decade at Microsoft in engineering and product management roles spanning cloud services and developer tools. Earlier in his career he was a founding member of the team behind Xbox's Forza franchise. He founded a charter school expanding access to education in rural America.

name: Jay Parikh
title: Executive Vice President, CoreAI
bio: Jay Parikh is a seasoned executive, board member, and advisor to some of the world’s fastest-growing and most successful consumer, developer, and enterprise technology companies. In October 2024, he joined Microsoft’s Senior Leadership Team as Executive Vice President of CoreAI, bringing deep expertise in engineering, product, and infrastructure to support CoreAI’s mission: Empower every developer to shape the future with AI. Beyond technology, Jay is committed to building talent, fostering culture, and accelerating customer value. Jay’s diverse background blends technical leadership with team-building, giving him a unique approach to scaling some of the world’s most iconic companies. As Vice President and Global Head of Engineering and Infrastructure at Facebook from 2009 to 2021, he led global teams that designed, developed, and operated the infrastructure powering Facebook’s products, supporting its growth from 300 million to more than 3 billion users. At other points in his career, Jay has held leadership roles at Lacework, Ning, Akamai Technologies, and NetGravity. Known for his inventive spirit, Jay holds more than 20 US patents.

name: John Maeda
title: CVP Engineering, GitHub Design and Microsoft CoreAI Design
bio: John is an American technologist and design leader who has spent his career translating between the worlds of computation, design, and business. It's a bridging act Wired once summed up this way: "Maeda is to design what Warren Buffett is to finance." He currently leads design across GitHub and Microsoft CoreAI as Corporate Vice President of Engineering, and serves on the board of directors of MillerKnoll. His path there runs through the MIT Media Lab, the presidency of the Rhode Island School of Design, a design partner role at Kleiner Perkins, and executive roles at Automattic, Publicis Sapient, and Everbridge. The author of five books, including The Laws of Simplicity and How to Speak Machine, he has seen his work enter the permanent collections of MoMA and the Cartier Foundation, and he was the first recipient of the White House National Design Award. Off the clock, he collects seashells whose patterns mimic Rule 30 of Wolfram's cellular automata, proof that even his beachcombing is computational.

name: Idan Gazit
title: Head of GitHub Next
bio: Idan leads GitHub Next, the birthplace of GitHub Copilot and many more prototypes that explore how AI will make software development faster, easier, safer, and more accessible for developers everywhere. As a hybrid designer and developer, his interests span a variety of fields. Idan is keenly interested in data display issues, typography, and color. You’re likely to hear him talk about the pit of success and the importance of good nouns. Idan was previously a principal engineer at Heroku and is an alumnus of the Django web framework’s core development team. He is a firm believer in the power of web technologies and is most at home in them. Though many evenings you can find him soldering a new keyboard while trying to get Rust to run on a microcontroller.

bio: Cassidy Williams (aka cassidoo) is Senior Director of Developer Advocacy at GitHub, where she helps developers build better with open source and modern developer tools. name: Martin Woodward
title: VP, Developer Relations
bio: Martin is the VP of developer relations at GitHub, helping developers and open source communities create delightful things. Prior to that role, he was part of the Microsoft team that built tooling for DevOps teams inside and outside the company, transforming how Microsoft builds software—by reshaping how it collaborates with open source communities and engages with developers. Martin was the original creator of the Microsoft organization on GitHub. He also helped set up the .NET Foundation and brought in companies like Amazon, Google, Samsung, and Red Hat to help drive its future direction. Martin joined Microsoft when it acquired his five-person startup—built on an Eclipse-based Java platform—and later served on the acquisition team when Microsoft acquired GitHub.

name: Yasuhiro Osaki
title: Software Engineer
bio: Yasuhiro is a Software Engineer at Sony, where he has spent over a decade driving GitHub adoption and serving as GitHub Owner across the organization. Sony’s development landscape spans embedded software to web and cloud applications, and he has developed enterprise-specific strategies for GitHub utilization at scale. In the past year alone, Yasuhiro helped grow GitHub Enterprise Cloud users from 4,000 to 7,000 and GitHub Copilot users from 900 to 4,000. He currently advises multiple organizations as a GitHub Enterprise Owner. He holds three GitHub Certifications (Actions, Admin, and GitHub Advanced Security) and recently spoke at GitHub Universe ’25 Recap Tokyo, receiving an audience rating of 4.38 out of 5.

name: Qianqian Ye
title: Director of Creative Technology and Adjunct Associate Professor
company: Processing Foundation, University of Southern California
bio: Qianqian (Q) Ye is a Chinese creative technologist, designer, and educator based in Los Angeles. As Director of Creative Technology at the Processing Foundation, they lead projects, programs, and partnerships that connect open-source technology, creative practice, and community. Qianqian has taught creative coding as an Adjunct Associate Professor in USC's Media Arts + Practice program since 2020. From 2021 to 2025, they served as p5.js Lead at the Processing Foundation, overseeing the design, development, and community stewardship of p5.js, an open-source coding tool for accessible, inclusive creative coding used by more than 5 million people worldwide. They have also been an Internet Archive DWeb Fellow, NYU ITP/IMA Project Fellow, and Senior Civic Media Fellow at the USC Annenberg Innovation Lab.

name: Mina Tawadrous
title: Associate Director, Product Management
bio: Mina leads Product in Platform Engineering at SiriusXM, where he works on developer productivity and experience, and on moving product decisions out of spreadsheets and into code. Before product management, he built games — a background that’s made him allergic to internal tools nobody wants to open. He’s previously spoken on “Assumptions as Code” and on how internal product management differs from its external counterpart. Across both, he’s made a habit of applying engineering rigor to the parts of product work that usually escape it. Based in Toronto, Mina is raising three kids, working through a graphic novel collection that keeps outgrowing its shelf, and maintaining an absurd yo-yo collection on the side.
